family_title: Parameter sharing, random bases, spectral transforms and extreme-efficiency adapters

methods.name: VeRA
methods.paper_title: VeRA: Vector-based Random Matrix Adaptation
methods.formula_latex: W = W_0 + \Lambda_b\, B\, \Lambda_d\, A,\quad B\in\mathbb{R}^{d_{out}\times r},\ A\in\mathbb{R}^{r\times d_{in}}\ \text{frozen, random (seeded), shared by all adapted layers};\ \Lambda_b=\mathrm{diag}(b),\ b\in\mathbb{R}^{d_{out}},\ \Lambda_d=\mathrm{diag}(d),\ d\in\mathbb{R}^{r}\ \text{trained per layer}
methods.trainable_params: d_{out} + r
methods.locus: any linear layer (paper: W_q, W_v of RoBERTa/GPT-2/Llama/ViT); one shared random pair sized to the largest layer
methods.structure: frozen shared random bases with trainable diagonal scalings: \Delta W = \mathrm{diag}(b)\,B\,\mathrm{diag}(d)\,A factors through a fixed random r-dimensional space; only the row scaling of B and the rank-channel scaling are learned
methods.mergeable_reason: Lambda_b B Lambda_d A is a fixed-shape matrix that can be added to W_0 after training.
methods.identity_at_init: b = 0 (so \Delta W = 0); d initialised to a constant (e.g. 0.1 or 1, a tunable hyper-parameter); A, B Kaiming-initialised and regenerated from an RNG seed, so only b, d and the seed are stored
methods.key_idea: Freeze one pair of random low-rank matrices shared by every layer and learn only two scaling vectors per layer, so per-layer storage is a vector instead of a matrix; random features plus learned scalings suffice for adaptation.
methods.results_note: Matches LoRA on GLUE (RoBERTa) and E2E (GPT-2) and in Llama 7B/13B instruction tuning while using an order of magnitude or more fewer trainable parameters (e.g. 18.4K vs 589.8K for RoBERTa-base at r=16 in its parameter table).

relations.note: reparameterises LoRA's B, A as frozen shared random matrices with trainable diagonal scalings
Tied-LoRA's framework recovers VeRA when tied A, B are random and frozen and only u, v are trained
Uni-LoRA writes VeRA as theta_D = P theta_d with a structured layer-wise projection
RandLoRA sums n VeRA-like scaled random products (scalings on rank and input columns rather than output rows) to reach full rank
contemporaneous random-basis compression of LoRA (ICLR 2024)

methods.name: PVeRA
methods.paper_title: PVeRA: Probabilistic Vector-Based Random Matrix Adaptation
methods.formula_latex: h = W_0x + \alpha\,\Lambda_b B\, z,\quad z = \mu + \epsilon\odot\sigma,\ \epsilon\sim\mathcal{N}(0,I),\quad [\mu;\sigma] = \Lambda_d A x;\ A\in\mathbb{R}^{2r\times d_{in}},\ B\in\mathbb{R}^{d_{out}\times r}\ \text{frozen random shared};\ d\in\mathbb{R}^{2r},\ b\in\mathbb{R}^{d_{out}}\ \text{trained};\ \mathcal{L}=\mathcal{L}_{task}+\beta\sum \mathrm{KL}(\mathcal{N}(\mu,\sigma^2)\,\|\,\mathcal{N}(0,I));\ \text{deterministic inference: } W = W_0 + \alpha\Lambda_b B\,\Lambda_{d_\mu}A_\mu
methods.trainable_params: d_{out} + 2r
methods.locus: linear layers (paper: W_q, W_v of ViT); shared random matrices as in VeRA
methods.structure: VeRA with a stochastic (VAE-style reparameterised) rank-r bottleneck: the r-dim code is sampled from a Gaussian whose mean and std are VeRA-style scaled random projections of x; KL prior on the code
methods.mergeable_reason: With mean (deterministic) inference z = mu the update is a fixed matrix that merges like VeRA; Monte-Carlo sampling mode at test time is input-dependent and cannot be merged.
methods.identity_at_init: b = 0 (HF: \lambda_b zeros), d = d_{initial} (0.1); so the adapter output is zero at init
methods.key_idea: Make VeRA's shared-random-basis bottleneck probabilistic so the adapter learns a distribution over adaptations, enabling uncertainty estimates while keeping VeRA's tiny footprint and mergeability.
methods.results_note: Outperforms VeRA and six other adapters on VTAB-1k with ViT backbones.

relations.note: same frozen shared random A, B and trainable scaling vectors, plus a reparameterised Gaussian bottleneck

methods.name: NOLA
methods.full_name: Compressing LoRA using Linear Combination of Random Basis
methods.paper_title: NOLA: Compressing LoRA using Linear Combination of Random Basis
methods.formula_latex: W = W_0 + \Big(\sum_{j=1}^{l}\beta_j B_j\Big)\Big(\sum_{i=1}^{k}\alpha_i A_i\Big),\quad B_j\in\mathbb{R}^{d_{out}\times r},\ A_i\in\mathbb{R}^{r\times d_{in}}\ \text{frozen pseudo-random (generated from a seed, optionally shared across layers)};\ \alpha\in\mathbb{R}^{k},\ \beta\in\mathbb{R}^{l}\ \text{trained}
methods.trainable_params: k + l\ \ (\text{independent of } r,\ d_{in},\ d_{out})
methods.locus: any linear layer (paper: attention projections of GPT-2, LLaMA-2, ViT)
methods.structure: LoRA factors constrained to the linear span of k (resp. l) frozen random basis matrices; \Delta W is bilinear in the two coefficient vectors and has rank \le r
methods.mergeable_reason: After training the two linear combinations are materialised, and their product BA is added to W_0.
methods.identity_at_init: Not specified in the paper; the official README example zero-initialises the coefficient vectors of a factor (\Delta W = 0). Bases are uniform U(-1,1) from a stored seed and are regenerated on the fly in forward/backward to save memory
methods.key_idea: Decouple the parameter count from rank and width (LoRA's rank-1 floor) by expressing each LoRA factor as a learned mixture of seeded random basis matrices, PRANC-style; only the seed and the mixture coefficients (optionally 4-bit quantised) are stored.
methods.results_note: On LLaMA-2 70B NOLA is about 20x more compact than the most compressed (rank-1) LoRA without accuracy loss; also matches LoRA on GPT-2 E2E and ViT few-shot classification with fewer parameters.

relations.note: reparameterises LoRA's A and B
random-subspace training (intrinsic dimension), restricted to the LoRA factor space; inspired by PRANC
our observation: (alpha, beta) -> (A, B) is linear, i.e. theta_D = P theta_d with a block-diagonal dense random P
contemporaneous random-basis compression of LoRA
RandLoRA compares against NOLA as a random-basis baseline

methods.name: RandLoRA
methods.full_name: RandLoRA: full-rank parameter-efficient fine-tuning with random bases
methods.paper_title: RandLoRA: Full-rank parameter-efficient fine-tuning of large models
methods.formula_latex: W = W_0 + \sum_{j=1}^{n} B_j\,\Lambda_j\,A\,\Gamma_j,\quad B_j\in\mathbb{R}^{d_{out}\times r},\ A\in\mathbb{R}^{r\times d_{in}}\ \text{frozen random (A shared by all terms; bases shared across layers)};\ \Lambda_j\in\mathbb{R}^{r\times r},\ \Gamma_j\in\mathbb{R}^{d_{in}\times d_{in}}\ \text{diagonal, trained};\ n=\min(d_{in},d_{out})/r\ \text{for a full-rank update (layer oriented so that } d_{in}=\min(d_{in},d_{out}))
methods.trainable_params: n\,(r + d_{in}) = \tfrac{d_{in}^2}{r} + d_{in}\quad (n = d_{in}/r,\ d_{in}=\min(d_{in},d_{out}))
methods.locus: any linear layer (paper: ViT/CLIP vision and text encoders, LLMs such as Qwen2, Phi3, Llama3)
methods.structure: sum of n rank-r terms, each a frozen random basis pair with trainable diagonal scalings on both the bottleneck (Lambda_j) and the input columns (Gamma_j); the sum has full rank min(d_in, d_out) with probability one
methods.mergeable_reason: The sum of scaled random products is a dense matrix added to W_0 after training.
methods.identity_at_init: \Lambda_j = 0 (HF: \lambda zeros, \gamma = 1/\max(\text{shape})), so \Delta W = 0
methods.key_idea: Separate the effect of parameter count from the effect of rank: combine many VeRA-like random low-rank terms with learned diagonal scalings to obtain full-rank updates at LoRA-like parameter budgets; the number of trainable parameters is inversely proportional to the basis rank.
methods.results_note: Full-rank updates help across vision, language and especially vision-language (CLIP) tasks, where RandLoRA significantly reduces and sometimes closes the gap between LoRA and full fine-tuning.

relations.note: a sum of VeRA-like scaled random products (diagonal scalings on the bottleneck and input columns) instead of a single one
both use random bases; RandLoRA targets full rank
matches LoRA's parameter budget while removing the rank bottleneck

methods.name: Intrinsic SAID
methods.paper_title: Intrinsic Dimensionality Explains the Effectiveness of Language Model Fine-Tuning
methods.formula_latex: \theta^{D}_{i} = \theta^{D}_{0,i} + \lambda_i\,\big(\theta^{d-m}M\big)_i,\quad M = H\,G\,\Pi\,H\,B\ \ (\text{Fastfood transform: Hadamard } H,\ \text{Gaussian diagonal } G,\ \text{permutation } \Pi,\ \pm1 \text{ diagonal } B;\ \text{frozen});\ \theta^{d-m}\in\mathbb{R}^{d-m},\ \lambda\in\mathbb{R}^{m}\ (\text{one scale per layer})\ \text{trained}
methods.trainable_params: d\ \text{for the whole model (e.g. } d\approx 200 \text{ reaches 90\% of full fine-tuning on MRPC with RoBERTa)}
methods.locus: the entire flattened parameter vector of the model (all layers), with layer-wise scaling
methods.structure: random linear subspace of the full parameter space: \Delta\theta = \mathrm{diag}(\lambda)\,P\,\theta_d with a structured random (Fastfood) projection P
methods.mergeable_reason: The projected update is a fixed parameter offset that can be added to theta_0.
methods.identity_at_init: \theta^{d} = 0 recovers the pretrained parameters exactly
methods.key_idea: Fine-tuning works in a tiny random subspace: optimise a d-dimensional vector projected into the full parameter space; the small d needed (intrinsic dimension) explains why huge models fine-tune well on little data. SAID adds per-layer scales.
methods.results_note: Optimising only about 200 parameters projected into RoBERTa's full space reaches 90% of full fine-tuning performance on MRPC; larger and longer-pretrained models have lower intrinsic dimension.

relations.note: LoRA cites the low intrinsic dimension finding as motivation; a low-rank factor space instead of a random linear subspace

methods.name: Tied-LoRA
methods.full_name: Tied Low-Rank Adaptation (weight tying + selective training)
methods.paper_title: Tied-LoRA: Enhancing parameter efficiency of LoRA with Weight Tying
methods.formula_latex: W_\ell = W_{0,\ell} + \Lambda_{v_\ell}\, B\, \Lambda_{u_\ell}\, A,\quad A\in\mathbb{R}^{r\times d_{in}},\ B\in\mathbb{R}^{d_{out}\times r}\ \text{tied (one copy shared by all layers)};\ \Lambda_{u_\ell}=\mathrm{diag}(u_\ell),\ u_\ell\in\mathbb{R}^{r},\ \Lambda_{v_\ell}=\mathrm{diag}(v_\ell),\ v_\ell\in\mathbb{R}^{d_{out}}\ \text{per layer};\ \text{each of } A,B,u,v \text{ is selectively trained or frozen (configs TL1--TL6; TL6 trains all)}
methods.trainable_params: \text{TL6: } r(d_{in}+d_{out})\ \text{once for all layers} + L\,(r + d_{out})\ \text{in total; per adapted matrix } \approx r + d_{out} + \tfrac{r(d_{in}+d_{out})}{L}
methods.locus: paper: the fused QKV projection (d x 3d) of every transformer layer; applicable to any linear layer
methods.structure: a single low-rank pair BA shared across depth, modulated per layer by diagonal scalings of its rows and rank channels; selective freezing yields a lattice of sub-configurations
methods.mergeable_reason: The low-rank path is linear, so each layer's Lambda_v B Lambda_u A can be merged into W_0.
methods.identity_at_init: TL6/TL2 (VeRA-like): A, B \sim \mathcal{N}, u = 1, v = 0; LoRA-like configs (TL3--TL5): A \sim \mathcal{N}, B = 0, u = v = 1; alpha set to r
methods.key_idea: Tie one LoRA pair across all layers and train only what is needed (shared factors and/or per-layer scaling vectors); a framework containing LoRA and VeRA as corners of the same design space.
methods.results_note: The TL6 configuration (trainable tied A, B plus per-layer u, v) is comparable to LoRA across five tasks with a fraction of the parameters, and surpasses LoRA on translation using 12.5% of its parameters; math reasoning favours plain LoRA.

relations.note: VeRA = tied, frozen random A, B with trainable u, v
untied A, B with Lambda = I recovers LoRA
ShareLoRA shares only one of the two factors
Uni-LoRA writes Tied-LoRA as a structured projection P

methods.name: ShareLoRA
methods.paper_title: ShareLoRA: Parameter Efficient and Robust Large Language Model Fine-tuning via Shared Low-Rank Adaptation
methods.formula_latex: \text{ShareA: } W_\ell = W_{0,\ell} + \alpha\, B_\ell\, A,\quad A\in\mathbb{R}^{r\times d_{in}}\ \text{shared by all layers},\ B_\ell\in\mathbb{R}^{d_{out}\times r}\ \text{per layer};\quad \text{ShareB: } \alpha\, B\, A_\ell;\quad \text{ShareAB: } \alpha\, B A\ \text{for every layer (all factors trained)}
methods.trainable_params: \text{ShareA: } r\,d_{out} + \tfrac{r\,d_{in}}{L}\ \text{per adapted matrix (i.e. } L r d_{out} + r d_{in} \text{ per module type)}
methods.locus: attention projections (Q, K, V, optionally sharing one down-projection across Q/K/V) and other linear layers of RoBERTa, GPT-2, LLaMA 1/2/3
methods.structure: LoRA in which one factor (the down-projection A, the up-projection B, or both) is a single matrix shared across depth; \Delta W_\ell = B_\ell A spans a common row space for all layers
methods.mergeable_reason: Each layer's B_l A is an ordinary low-rank matrix that can be added to W_0.
methods.identity_at_init: Inherits LoRA initialisation (up-projection zero, so Delta W = 0); not discussed separately in the paper
methods.key_idea: Share LoRA's down- (or up-) projection across all layers: the shared subspace removes redundancy, roughly halves parameters or more, and acts as a regulariser that improves robustness and continual-learning transfer.
methods.results_note: 44%-96% fewer trainable parameters than LoRA with maintained performance on RoBERTa, GPT-2 and LLaMA 1/2/3, and up to 1.2% higher average accuracy in zero/few-shot and continual fine-tuning settings.

relations.note: shares one LoRA factor across layers
Tied-LoRA ties both factors and adds scaling vectors; ShareAB with no scalings is a Tied-LoRA corner
Lily shares A locally and B globally with a router

methods.name: PRoLoRA
methods.paper_title: PRoLoRA: Partial Rotation Empowers More Parameter-Efficient LoRA
methods.formula_latex: W = W_0 + BA,\quad B = \big[\,B_u\ \big|\ \big(B_0;\,\mathrm{Roll}(B_0,s_B);\dots;\mathrm{Roll}(B_0,(n{-}1)s_B)\big)\big],\quad A = \Big[\,A_u;\ \big(A_0\,|\,\mathrm{Roll}(A_0,s_A)\,|\cdots|\,\mathrm{Roll}(A_0,(m{-}1)s_A)\big)\Big];\ A_u\in\mathbb{R}^{u\times d_{in}},\ B_u\in\mathbb{R}^{d_{out}\times u}\ \text{(unshared ranks)},\ A_0\in\mathbb{R}^{(r-u)\times d_{in}/m},\ B_0\in\mathbb{R}^{d_{out}/n\times(r-u)}\ \text{trained};\ \mathrm{Roll} = \text{cyclic shift along the rank dimension}
methods.trainable_params: u\,(d_{in}+d_{out}) + (r-u)\Big(\tfrac{d_{in}}{m} + \tfrac{d_{out}}{n}\Big)
methods.locus: any linear layer (paper: all linear layers of LLaMA-2 / Tulu instruction tuning)
methods.structure: intra-layer sharing: each LoRA factor is a broadcast of one small chunk along the hidden dimension, the copies differentiated by rank-dimension cyclic permutations, plus u unshared ranks; \Delta W is block-structured with blocks related by rank permutations
methods.mergeable_reason: The expanded B and A are ordinary matrices, so BA merges into W_0 exactly as in LoRA.
methods.identity_at_init: B = 0 (whole matrix); A_u Kaiming-uniform and the shared chunk A_0 with a rectified Kaiming bound computed from the full hidden size d_in so both parts have equal scale
methods.key_idea: Reuse parameters inside a layer: broadcast one chunk of each LoRA factor across the hidden dimension (more rank per parameter) and break the resulting repetition with cheap rotations and a few unshared ranks; a strict superset of LoRA.
methods.results_note: With half the trainable parameters of LoRA, PRoLoRA still outperforms LoRA on multiple instruction-tuning benchmarks and scales to larger LLMs.

relations.note: u = r (or m = n = 1) recovers LoRA
intra-layer instead of inter-layer sharing; not restricted by equal weight shapes
MoS builds on PRoLoRA-like intra-layer sharing and adds VeRA-like inter-layer sharing
MiSS also builds Delta W by tiling one shard

methods.name: MoS
methods.paper_title: MoS: Unleashing Parameter Efficiency of Low-Rank Adaptation with Mixture of Shards
methods.formula_latex: W_\ell = W_{0,\ell} + B_\ell A_\ell,\quad B_\ell = \mathrm{Route}^{c}\big([B^{pub}, B^{pri}],\, I^{b}_\ell\big),\quad A_\ell = \mathrm{Route}^{r}\big([A^{pub}, A^{pri}],\, I^{a}_\ell\big);\ \text{each rank vector of } A_\ell, B_\ell \text{ is the concatenation of } l \text{ shards retrieved from global pools by fixed random index matrices } I_\ell;\ \text{pools trained, indices frozen; private shards are used by one layer only}
methods.trainable_params: \approx e\,(d_{in}+d_{out})\ \text{per adapted matrix on average (global pools of size } eL(d_{in}+d_{out}) \text{ per linear-layer type), while each layer uses rank } r > e
methods.locus: all linear-layer types of LLaMA-2/3 (one global pool per layer type)
methods.structure: global inter- and intra-layer sharing: LoRA factor vectors are assembled from shards of shared public/private pools via subset selection, pair dissociation (separate pools for A and B), vector sharding and shard privatisation; routing is index-based and input-independent
methods.mergeable_reason: Indices are fixed, so after training each layer's B_l A_l is a fixed low-rank matrix that merges into W_0.
methods.identity_at_init: public and private B pools zero-initialised (\Delta W = 0); A pools with PRoLoRA-style rectified Kaiming bounds; index matrices sampled once at random
methods.key_idea: Pure sharing across layers hurts because all layers get the same update; cheap differentiation strategies (random subsets, dissociated A/B pools, shards, private shards) restore diversity while keeping the high sharing ratio.
methods.results_note: About 8x parameter savings relative to standard LoRA at matched performance on instruction-tuning benchmarks (MMLU, BBH, GSM8K, etc.), with ablations confirming each differentiation component.

relations.note: adopts intra-layer chunk sharing and rectified initialisation
adopts inter-layer sharing; replaces random scaling by subset selection
pure sharing (all pool vectors used in every block) is a tied LoRA without scaling vectors
both compose LoRA vectors from a global bank; MoS uses fixed hard indices, VB-LoRA learned top-k mixtures

methods.name: VB-LoRA
methods.paper_title: VB-LoRA: Extreme Parameter Efficient Fine-Tuning with Vector Banks
methods.formula_latex: W = W_0 + BA,\quad \text{every length-}b\text{ sub-vector } u \text{ of every column of } B \text{ and row of } A:\ u = \sum_{s=1}^{h} w_s(\sigma)\,\alpha_s,\ \ w(\sigma) = \mathrm{Softmax}\big(\mathrm{TopK}(\sigma,k)\big);\ \text{bank } \{\alpha_s\in\mathbb{R}^{b}\}_{s=1}^{h}\ \text{shared by all modules and layers (trained)},\ \sigma\in\mathbb{R}^{h}\ \text{logits per sub-vector (trained)}
methods.trainable_params: \text{training: } \tfrac{r(d_{in}+d_{out})}{b}\,h\ \text{logits per matrix} + hb\ \text{shared};\ \ \text{stored } (k=2,\ \text{uint8 indices}): \tfrac{3}{2}\,\tfrac{r(d_{in}+d_{out})}{b}\ \text{per matrix} + hb\ \text{shared}
methods.locus: any linear layer, sharing across modules and layers (paper: query/value or all linear layers of RoBERTa, GPT-2, Llama2, Mistral, Gemma)
methods.structure: divide-and-share: LoRA's rank-one component vectors are split into sub-vectors, each a sparse top-k convex combination (simplex-constrained) of a globally shared vector bank -- a hierarchical, constrained CP/tensor factorisation spanning the whole model
methods.mergeable_reason: After training the logits are discarded, the selected mixtures define fixed B, A, and BA merges into W_0.
methods.identity_at_init: Not exact: bank \sim U(-0.02, 0.02) and logits \sim \mathcal{N}(0, 0.1^2) (HF defaults), so \Delta W is small but non-zero; an all-zero bank is avoided because it would give zero gradients
methods.key_idea: Treat all LoRA parameters of a model as sub-vectors drawn from one small learned vector bank via differentiable sparse top-k admixture, so storage stops scaling with model width, depth and number of modules.
methods.results_note: On Llama2-13B instruction tuning VB-LoRA uses only 0.4% of LoRA's stored parameters yet scores higher on MT-Bench; it also outperforms baselines on GLUE, E2E and GSM8K/MATH (Mistral-7B, Gemma-7B).

relations.note: global reparameterisation of LoRA factors
fewer stored parameters than VeRA at comparable quality
finer-grained, learned sharing
Uni-LoRA writes VB-LoRA as a trainable projection P from the bank to theta_D
compared on GSM8K/MATH

methods.name: Uni-LoRA
methods.full_name: Uni-LoRA: one vector for all LoRA parameters via an isometric projection
methods.paper_title: Uni-LoRA: One Vector is All You Need
methods.formula_latex: \theta_D = P\,\theta_d,\quad \theta_D = \mathrm{Concat}_{\ell}\big(\mathrm{vec}(B^{\ell}),\mathrm{vec}(A^{\ell})\big)\in\mathbb{R}^{D},\ D=\sum_\ell r\,(d^{\ell}_{in}+d^{\ell}_{out}),\quad W_\ell = W_{0,\ell} + B^{\ell}A^{\ell};\ P\in\mathbb{R}^{D\times d}\ \text{frozen: each row one-hot at a uniformly random column, column } j \text{ scaled to } 1/\sqrt{n_j};\ \theta_d\in\mathbb{R}^{d}\ \text{trained (a single vector for the whole model)}
methods.trainable_params: d\ \text{for the whole model (independent of } L,\ d_{in},\ d_{out},\ r)
methods.locus: all LoRA-adapted modules of the model jointly (global, cross-layer)
methods.structure: global random isometric projection from one vector to all LoRA factors: a random partition of the D LoRA entries into d groups, each group sharing one (1/\sqrt{n_j}-scaled) value; the projection framework theta_D = P theta_d also expresses LoRA (P=I), Tied-LoRA, VeRA, LoRA-XS and VB-LoRA
methods.mergeable_reason: theta_d determines fixed B, A for every layer, and each BA merges into W_0.
methods.identity_at_init: Not exact: \theta_d \sim U(-0.02, 0.02) (HF default; zeros avoided to prevent vanishing gradients), so B, A are small and \Delta W = BA is near zero but non-zero
methods.key_idea: All parameter-efficient LoRA variants are projections of a low-dimensional vector into LoRA's parameter space and differ only in the projection matrix; a global, uniform, isometric random-grouping projection gives maximal cross-layer sharing at negligible cost (matching Fastfood).
methods.results_note: Matches or outperforms state-of-the-art LoRA variants on GLUE, mathematical reasoning (GSM8K/MATH) and instruction tuning while training a single vector for the whole LLM; the random-grouping projection matches Fastfood at much lower cost.

relations.note: VeRA is a structured layer-wise projection in the Uni-LoRA framework
Tied-LoRA corresponds to a tying projection
VB-LoRA corresponds to a trainable projection
LoRA-XS corresponds to a fixed SVD-based projection
intrinsic-dimension random projections (Fastfood) applied to LoRA's parameter space
MoSA applies the same equal-size random grouping directly to Delta W entries instead of LoRA factor entries

methods.name: Lily
methods.paper_title: Low-Rank Interconnected Adaptation across Layers
methods.formula_latex: h_\ell = W_{0,\ell}x + \Big(\sum_{e=1}^{N_e} s_{\ell,e}(x)\,B^{e}\Big)A_{g(\ell)}\,x,\quad s_\ell(x) = \mathrm{softmax}\Big(\sum_{t=1}^{N} R_\ell\,A_{g(\ell)}x_t\Big);\ A_{g}\in\mathbb{R}^{r\times d_{in}}\ \text{shared by a block of neighbouring layers},\ B^{e}\in\mathbb{R}^{d_{out}\times r}\ \text{global experts shared by all layers},\ R_\ell\in\mathbb{R}^{N_e\times r}\ \text{router; all trained}
methods.trainable_params: \approx \tfrac{L}{g}\,r\,d_{in} + N_e\,r\,d_{out} + L\,N_e\,r\ \text{per module type over } L \text{ layers (g layers share one } A)
methods.locus: targeted linear layers (e.g. q/v projections) of Transformers and Mamba/Vim models; sharing within each target type
methods.structure: hierarchical cross-layer sharing: locally shared down-projections and globally shared up-projection experts mixed by a sequence-level data-dependent router, giving each layer a higher-rank, input-dependent BA
methods.mergeable_reason: The mixture weights over B experts depend on the input sequence, so there is no single static Delta W to fold into W_0.
methods.identity_at_init: A Kaiming-uniform, all B experts zero, so the adapter output is zero at init (HF default)
methods.key_idea: Replace per-layer (A, B) pairs by a few shared adapters of much higher rank: A shared among neighbouring layers, B experts shared model-wide and mixed by a router, letting each layer draw on information from all layers at the same parameter budget.
methods.results_note: Improves over LoRA and other PEFT methods across NLU, commonsense reasoning, vision (VTAB) and Mamba-based models at equal or lower parameter budgets.

relations.note: both share LoRA factors across layers; Lily adds expert routing
shared-A, multiple-B structure, but Lily shares B experts across layers
both raise per-layer rank through cross-layer sharing

methods.name: RaSA
methods.paper_title: RaSA: Rank-Sharing Low-Rank Adaptation
methods.formula_latex: W_i = W_{0,i} + \big[\tilde B_i\ \ B_S\big]\, D_i \begin{bmatrix}\tilde A_i\\ A_S\end{bmatrix},\quad \tilde B_i\in\mathbb{R}^{d_{out}\times(r-k)},\ \tilde A_i\in\mathbb{R}^{(r-k)\times d_{in}}\ \text{layer-specific};\ B_S\in\mathbb{R}^{d_{out}\times Lk},\ A_S\in\mathbb{R}^{Lk\times d_{in}}\ \text{shared rank pool (k ranks contributed by each layer)};\ D_i\ \text{diagonal } (r-k+Lk)\ \text{per layer; all trained}
methods.trainable_params: r\,(d_{in}+d_{out}) + (r - k + Lk)\ \text{per adapted matrix (same as LoRA plus a diagonal)}
methods.locus: all linear layers of the LLM (assumes equal shapes across layers; e.g. Llama, Mistral)
methods.structure: partial rank sharing: \Delta W_i = \tilde B_i D_i^{(1)} \tilde A_i + B_S D_i^{(2)} A_S, a private rank-(r-k) term plus a shared rank-Lk pool reweighted per layer by a trainable diagonal; effective rank r - k + Lk
methods.mergeable_reason: For each layer the update is a fixed low-rank matrix that merges into W_0.
methods.identity_at_init: \tilde B_i = 0, B_S = 0; \tilde A_i, A_S Kaiming; D_i = \tfrac{\alpha}{2(r-k)} on private and \tfrac{\alpha}{2Lk} on shared ranks
methods.key_idea: Pool k ranks from every layer into a shared rank pool that all layers reuse with layer-specific diagonal weights, raising effective rank by (L-1)k at LoRA's parameter cost; its minimum reconstruction error is provably no worse than LoRA's.
methods.results_note: Significantly improves over LoRA and other variants on challenging code-generation and mathematical-reasoning fine-tuning at the same parameter budget.

relations.note: k = 0 recovers LoRA
per-layer diagonal scaling of shared factors (as in VeRA/Tied-LoRA) combined with private LoRA ranks
cross-layer sharing of LoRA rank vectors
cross-layer sharing to raise effective rank

methods.name: FacT
methods.paper_title: FacT: Factor-Tuning for Lightweight Adaptation on Vision Transformer

methods.structure: tensor-train / Tucker factorisation of the stacked update tensor: shared row and column bases U, V across all layers with a tiny per-matrix core (TT) or a shared core with per-matrix mixing weights (Tucker); LoRA is the Matrix-Batch format

methods.name: LoRA-XS
methods.full_name: Low-Rank Adaptation with eXtremely Small number of parameters
methods.paper_title: LoRA-XS: Low-Rank Adaptation with Extremely Small Number of Parameters
methods.formula_latex: W = W_0 + U_r\,R\,\Sigma_r V_r^{\top},\quad W_0 = U\Sigma V^{\top}\ (U_r, \Sigma_r, V_r:\ \text{top-}r \text{ truncated SVD, frozen}),\ R\in\mathbb{R}^{r\times r}\ \text{trained}\ \ (\text{paper, row-vector convention: } h = xW + xARB,\ A = U_r\Sigma_r,\ B = V_r^{\top};\ \text{equivalently } U_r\Sigma_r R' V_r^{\top} \text{ since } \Sigma_r \text{ is invertible})
methods.locus: any linear layer (paper: attention and MLP projections of RoBERTa, Mistral, Gemma, LLaMA)
methods.structure: a trainable r x r core sandwiched between frozen top-r singular subspaces of W_0 (Tucker-2 core); \Delta W lives in \mathrm{span}(U_r) \otimes \mathrm{span}(V_r)
methods.mergeable_reason: U_r R Sigma_r V_r^T is a fixed matrix that merges into W_0.
methods.identity_at_init: Near-identity, not exact: R \sim \mathcal{N}(0,\sigma^2) with \sigma = 10^{-5}
methods.key_idea: Freeze LoRA's factors at the SVD of the pretrained weight and train only a small r x r mixing matrix between them, removing LoRA's width-proportional parameter floor (as few as one parameter per module).
methods.results_note: Outperforms or matches LoRA and VeRA on GLUE, GSM8K, MATH and commonsense reasoning while reducing storage by over 100x for 7B models.

relations.note: uses principal singular subspaces of W_0, but freezes them
replaces random frozen factors by SVD factors and per-layer vectors by an r x r core
our observation: SVFT with M supported on a dense top-left r x r block (up to the invertible Sigma_r reparameterisation)

methods.name: LoRA-SB
methods.paper_title: Initialization using Update Approximation is a Silver Bullet for Extremely Efficient Low-Rank Fine-Tuning
methods.formula_latex: W = W_0 + s\,B\,R\,A,\quad (B, R, A) \leftarrow \mathrm{truncSVD}_r(\Delta W_{avg}):\ B = U_r\Sigma_r,\ A = V_r^{\top},\ R = I/s;\quad \Delta W_{avg} = -\eta\,\mathrm{sign}\Big(\sum_{i\le n}\nabla_W\mathcal{L}(W_0, x_i)\Big);\ B, A\ \text{frozen},\ R\in\mathbb{R}^{r\times r}\ \text{trained}
methods.locus: any linear layer (paper: attention and MLP projections of Mistral-7B, Gemma, LLaMA, RoBERTa)
methods.structure: LoRA-XS architecture (frozen B, A with trainable r x r core) whose frozen bases are the top-r singular subspaces of an estimated first full fine-tuning step instead of W_0
methods.mergeable_reason: sBRA is a fixed low-rank matrix after training.
methods.identity_at_init: Not identity by design: at init sBRA = \mathrm{truncSVD}_r(\Delta W_{avg}), i.e. the model starts from a rank-r approximation of one AdamW full fine-tuning step computed from about n=50 batches
methods.key_idea: With frozen outer factors the subspace is everything, so initialise it from the first full-fine-tuning update; then the equivalent gradient sB g_R A optimally approximates full fine-tuning at every step and needs no scaling-factor tuning.
methods.results_note: Exceeds LoRA while using 27-90x fewer trainable parameters on mathematical reasoning, commonsense reasoning and GLUE, and comprehensively outperforms LoRA-XS.

relations.note: same architecture, different (gradient-based) choice of frozen subspace
both initialise from gradient information; LoRA-SB freezes the resulting bases
both train only a tiny core inside frozen bases

methods.name: TinyLoRA
methods.full_name: TinyLoRA (LoRA-XS with a random-projected, tied trainable core)
methods.paper_title: Learning to Reason in 13 Parameters
methods.formula_latex: W = W_0 + U_r\Sigma_r\Big(\sum_{i=1}^{u} v_i\,P_i\Big)V_r^{\top},\quad U_r,\Sigma_r,V_r\ \text{truncated SVD of } W_0\ (\text{frozen}),\ P_i\in\mathbb{R}^{r\times r}\ \text{fixed random},\ v\in\mathbb{R}^{u}\ \text{trained and optionally tied across } n_{tie} \text{ modules}
methods.trainable_params: u\ \text{per module, or } \tfrac{n\,m\,u}{n_{tie}} \text{ in total for } n \text{ layers and } m \text{ modules per layer (as few as 1)}
methods.locus: all seven linear projections per block (q, k, v, o, up, down, gate) of Qwen2.5 / LLaMA-3 models
methods.structure: LoRA-XS core replaced by a random linear image of a u-dimensional vector (NOLA-style random basis inside the SVD sandwich), with the vector tied across modules and layers
methods.mergeable_reason: The update is a fixed dense matrix per module; the authors merge it at every RL step for vLLM inference.
methods.identity_at_init: HF default initialises v = 0 (adapter is a no-op); a uniform small init is optional. The paper does not advocate a specific initialisation
methods.key_idea: Even rank-1 LoRA is far larger than needed for RL-based reasoning: project a handful of shared parameters through fixed random matrices into LoRA-XS cores, scaling updates down to a single parameter.
methods.results_note: Trains Qwen2.5-7B-Instruct to 91% GSM8K accuracy with 13 trained parameters (26 bytes in bf16) using GRPO, and recovers about 90% of the gains with 1000x fewer parameters on MATH500/AIME/AMC; SFT needs 100-1000x larger updates for the same performance.

methods.name: LaMDA
methods.full_name: Large Model Fine-Tuning via Spectrally Decomposed Low-Dimensional Adaptation
methods.paper_title: LaMDA: Large Model Fine-Tuning via Spectrally Decomposed Low-Dimensional Adaptation
methods.formula_latex: W = \big(W_0 - U_r\Sigma_r V_r^{\top}\big) + \alpha\,U_r\,S\,\Sigma_r V_r^{\top},\quad \Sigma_r V_r^{\top}\ (\text{PMA, down-projection) frozen},\ S\in\mathbb{R}^{r\times r}\ (\text{LDA}) \text{ trained},\ U_r\ (\text{PMB, up-projection) trainable early and frozen row by row on a linear schedule}\ \ (\text{paper, row-vector convention: } Y = XW + \alpha XASB,\ A = U[:,{:}r]\Sigma_r,\ B = V[:,{:}r]^{\top})
methods.trainable_params: r^{2}\ (+\ \text{a decreasing number of rows of the up-projection during the early phase; LaMDA++ adapts } r \text{ per layer})
methods.locus: any linear layer (paper: DeBERTa-V3, BART, GPT-2, LLaMA-2 attention/MLP projections)
methods.structure: PiSSA-style residual split with a trainable r x r core between frozen spectral factors; the up-projection is progressively frozen, so late training is a pure r^2-parameter basis change
methods.mergeable_reason: After training the residual and the adapter path are fixed matrices that sum to a single weight.
methods.identity_at_init: S = I_r and the main path holds the residual W_0 - U_r\Sigma_rV_r^{\top}, so W = W_0 at init (for alpha = 1)

relations.note: contemporaneous r x r core between frozen SVD factors

methods.name: LoRA-Mini
methods.full_name: LoRA-Mini: Adaptation Matrices Decomposition and Selective Training
methods.paper_title: LoRA-Mini : Adaptation Matrices Decomposition and Selective Training
methods.formula_latex: W = W_0 + P\,C\,D\,Q,\quad P\in\mathbb{R}^{d_{out}\times b},\ Q\in\mathbb{R}^{a\times d_{in}}\ \text{frozen outer (auxiliary) matrices};\ C\in\mathbb{R}^{b\times r},\ D\in\mathbb{R}^{r\times a}\ \text{trained inner matrices}\ \ (\text{paper: } h = (W + A_{aux}A_{train}B_{train}B_{aux})x)

methods.identity_at_init: The paper reports Kaiming initialisation for all four matrices and does not state a zero-initialised factor, so an exact identity at init is not guaranteed as described

methods.results_note: Up to 20x fewer trainable parameters than LoRA with comparable GLUE and WMT16 En-Ro translation performance.

methods.name: SVFT
methods.paper_title: SVFT: Parameter-Efficient Fine-Tuning with Singular Vectors
methods.formula_latex: W = U(\Sigma + M)V^{\top} = W_0 + U M V^{\top},\quad W_0 = U\Sigma V^{\top}\ (U, V \text{ frozen}),\ M\ \text{sparse with a fixed pattern } \Omega\ (\text{Plain: diagonal; Banded: } |i-j|\le z;\ \text{Random; Top-}k \text{ by } |u_i^{\top}v_j|)\ \text{trained}
methods.trainable_params: |\Omega|\ \ (\min(d_{in},d_{out}) \text{ for Plain}; \approx (2z{+}1)\min(d_{in},d_{out}) \text{ for Banded})
methods.locus: any linear layer (paper: Gemma/LLaMA attention and MLP for math and commonsense, DeBERTa on GLUE, ViT)
methods.structure: sparse core in W_0's own singular-vector basis: \Delta W = \sum_{(i,j)\in\Omega} m_{ij}\,u_i v_j^{\top}, a sparse combination of outer products of W_0's singular vectors (weight-dependent dictionary); rank \le \min(|\Omega|, \min(d_{in},d_{out}))
methods.mergeable_reason: U M V^T is a dense matrix that can be added to W_0.
methods.identity_at_init: Not specified in the paper; the official code initialises the trainable coefficients with Kaiming-normal noise scaled by sigmoid(gate) with gate = 0 (factor 0.5), so Delta W is small but non-zero
methods.key_idea: Make the structure of Delta W depend on W itself: update the weight as a sparse combination of outer products of its own singular vectors, training only the coefficients; expressivity is tuned by the sparsity pattern.
methods.results_note: Recovers up to 96% of full fine-tuning performance while training only 0.006%-0.25% of parameters, versus at most 85% for prior methods using 0.03%-0.8%.

relations.note: our observation: a dense top-left r x r block of M gives the LoRA-XS form

methods.name: FRoD
methods.full_name: Full-Rank Efficient Fine-Tuning with Rotational Degrees
methods.paper_title: FRoD: Full-Rank Efficient Fine-Tuning with Rotational Degrees for Fast Convergence
methods.formula_latex: W_i = U_i\big(\Sigma_i + S_i\big)V^{\top},\quad V\ \text{global orthonormal basis shared by all layers (hierarchical joint QR + eigendecomposition of the stacked weights)},\ U_i\ \text{per-layer factor (frozen)};\ \Sigma_i\ \text{diagonal strengths and } S_i\ \text{random-pattern sparse off-diagonal perturbation (density } s)\ \text{trained}
methods.trainable_params: d_{in} + s\,d_{in}^{2}\ \text{per adapted matrix (diagonal plus sparse off-diagonal entries of an } d_{in}\times d_{in} \text{ core)}
methods.locus: selected linear layers of ViT, LLaMA-style and encoder models (grouped by layer category for the joint decomposition)
methods.structure: cross-layer shared latent basis with a per-layer diagonal-plus-sparse core: on-axis updates rescale generalised singular values, sparse off-diagonal entries inject small rotations; full-rank updates
methods.mergeable_reason: U_i(Sigma_i + S_i)V^T is a dense matrix that replaces W_i at no extra inference cost.
methods.identity_at_init: S_i = 0 and U_i Sigma_i V^T reconstructs W_i (maximum error below 1e-5), so the model is essentially unchanged at init; the joint decomposition is a costly one-off initialisation
methods.key_idea: Extract a basis shared by all layers via a hierarchical joint decomposition, then fine-tune only per-layer scaling factors plus sparse off-diagonal rotations in that basis, giving full-rank updates and fast convergence.

methods.name: MiSS (Bone / DiSHA)
methods.full_name: Matrix Shard Sharing (earlier: Block-Affine Adaptation, Dimension-Sharding Adaptation)
methods.paper_title: MiSS: Revisiting the Trade-off in LoRA with an Efficient Shard-Sharing Structure
methods.formula_latex: W = W_0 + \mathrm{expand}(D);\ \text{efficient form: } \Delta W = \mathbf{1}_g^{\top}\otimes D = [\,D\ D\ \cdots\ D\,],\ \text{i.e. } \Delta W x = D\sum_{i=1}^{g} x^{(i)},\quad D\in\mathbb{R}^{d_{out}\times r}\ \text{trained},\ g = d_{in}/r,\ x^{(i)}\in\mathbb{R}^{r}\ \text{the } i\text{-th input block};\ \text{Bat variant (Bone): } \Delta W_{blk} = W_{0,blk}\,D_{blk} + D_{blk}
methods.trainable_params: d_{out}\,r\ \ (\text{'mini' variant: } \text{mini\_r}\cdot r)
methods.locus: any linear layer (paper: LLaMA-2/3, Mistral, RWKV, RoBERTa)
methods.structure: shard sharing: \Delta W is a horizontal tiling of one trainable d_{out} x r shard (rank \le r) -- equivalently LoRA with trainable B = D and a frozen deterministic summing projection A = \mathbf{1}_g^{\top}\otimes I_r (our observation); Bat adds a weight-guided block-affine term
methods.mergeable_reason: The tiled (or block-affine) update is a fixed matrix once D is trained.
methods.identity_at_init: D = 0 (single trainable matrix initialised to zero), so Delta W = 0
methods.key_idea: Updating many shards of the weight with a single shared small matrix keeps LoRA's low-rank character while removing one factor, which speeds convergence and cuts memory and FLOPs (input block-summation instead of a down-projection).
methods.results_note: Outperforms LoRA and its variants on NLU/NLG benchmarks while lying on a favourable performance-memory-compute Pareto frontier; in the HF PEFT benchmark it replaced Bone as the recommended variant.

relations.note: our observation: LoRA with B = D trained and A frozen to a block-summing matrix
both freeze the down-projection; MiSS uses a deterministic summing projection

methods.name: MoSA
methods.paper_title: MoSA: Mosaic Shared Adaptation of Large Language Models
methods.formula_latex: W = W_0 + \sum_{k=1}^{K}\lambda_k M_k,\quad M_k\in\{0,1\}^{d_{out}\times d_{in}}\ \text{disjoint masks of a fixed balanced random tessellation (frozen)},\ \lambda\in\mathbb{R}^{K}\ \text{trained}
methods.trainable_params: K\ \ (\text{set to } r(d_{in}+d_{out}) \text{ to match a rank-}r \text{ LoRA budget})
methods.locus: any linear layer (paper: LLaMA-2-7B, LLaMA-3-8B)
methods.structure: random weight sharing (hashing trick) on the update: every entry of \Delta W is tied to one of K scalars via a fixed balanced random partition; generally full rank; gradient of \lambda_k is the group sum of \nabla_W\mathcal{L}
methods.mergeable_reason: Broadcasting the scalars gives a dense Delta W that is added to W_0 for zero-overhead inference.
methods.identity_at_init: Not specified in the extracted text (low confidence); zero-initialising lambda gives Delta W = 0 and, unlike two-factor schemes, still yields non-zero gradients
methods.key_idea: Replace low-rank factorisation by randomised, non-local sharing of individual update entries; equal-size random groups provably minimise the expected deviation from the unconstrained gradient and act as a regulariser.
methods.results_note: Matches or surpasses strong PEFT baselines (LoRA, DoRA, MoRA, HiRA) under strictly matched budgets on commonsense reasoning, ConvAI2 dialogue and MetaMathQA to GSM8K.

relations.note: same balanced random grouping idea, applied to Delta W entries rather than LoRA factor entries
high-rank update at LoRA's parameter count

methods.name: FourierFT
methods.paper_title: Parameter-Efficient Fine-Tuning with Discrete Fourier Transform
methods.formula_latex: W = W_0 + \alpha\,\mathrm{Re}\big(\mathcal{F}^{-1}_{2D}(F)\big),\quad F_{jk} = c_l \text{ if } (j,k) = (E_{0,l},E_{1,l}),\ 0 \text{ otherwise};\ E\in\mathbb{N}^{2\times n}\ \text{random spectral entries, frozen and shared by all layers},\ c\in\mathbb{R}^{n}\ \text{trained per layer},\ \alpha \text{ shared scale}
methods.trainable_params: n\ \ (\text{plus the shared frozen entry matrix } E)
methods.locus: any linear layer (paper: query and value projections of RoBERTa, GPT-2, LLaMA-2, ViT)
methods.structure: sparse coefficients in the 2-D Fourier basis: \Delta W = \alpha\,\mathrm{Re}\sum_{l} c_l\, \phi_{E_l}, where each 2-D DFT basis matrix \phi_{(j,k)} is an outer product of two Fourier vectors (real part rank \le 2); fixed dictionary, shared random support
methods.mergeable_reason: The inverse DFT of the learned sparse spectrum is a dense matrix that can be added to W_0.
methods.identity_at_init: Paper: c \sim \mathcal{N}(0,1), so \Delta W is small (IDFT normalisation) but non-zero; HF PEFT: init_weights=True zero-initialises the spectrum (exact identity), default False keeps the Gaussian
methods.key_idea: Treat Delta W as a spatial-domain signal and learn only a few of its spectral coefficients at random frequencies shared across layers; the expressive orthogonal Fourier basis recovers useful updates with far fewer parameters than LoRA.
methods.results_note: In LLaMA2-7B instruction tuning FourierFT surpasses LoRA with 0.064M trainable parameters versus LoRA's 33.5M; comparable or better than LoRA on GLUE, E2E and ViT image classification with fewer parameters.

relations.note: replaces the low-rank structure with a sparse spectral one

methods.name: WaveFT
methods.paper_title: Exploring Sparsity for Parameter Efficient Fine Tuning Using Wavelets
methods.formula_latex: W = W_0 + \lambda\,\mathrm{IDWT}_{2D}(C),\quad C\in\mathbb{R}^{d_{out}\times d_{in}}\ \text{sparse: exactly } p \text{ entries chosen uniformly at random are trainable, the rest fixed at } 0

methods.name: SSH
methods.full_name: Sparse Spectrum Adaptation via Discrete Hartley Transformation
methods.paper_title: SSH: Sparse Spectrum Adaptation via Discrete Hartley Transformation
methods.formula_latex: W = W_0 + \alpha\,\mathcal{H}^{-1}(\Delta H),\quad \Delta H \text{ sparse with } n \text{ trainable entries: } \lfloor\delta n\rfloor \text{ at the highest-energy frequencies of } \mathcal{H}(W_0),\ \text{the rest at random frequencies};\ \mathcal{H} = \text{2-D discrete Hartley transform (real, self-inverse up to scale)}

methods.name: LoCA
methods.paper_title: LoCA: Location-Aware Cosine Adaptation for Parameter-Efficient Fine-Tuning
methods.formula_latex: W = W_0 + \alpha\,C^{\top}\mathcal{S}(a, l)\,D = W_0 + \alpha\sum_{i=1}^{\mathcal{B}} a_i\,C_{l^1_i,:}^{\top}\,D_{l^2_i,:},\quad C\in\mathbb{R}^{d_{out}\times d_{out}},\ D\in\mathbb{R}^{d_{in}\times d_{in}}\ \text{DCT matrices (fixed)};\ a\in\mathbb{R}^{\mathcal{B}} \text{ coefficients and their 2-D locations } l \text{ trained (locations via finite-difference gradient estimates)}

methods.name: C3A
methods.paper_title: Parameter-Efficient Fine-Tuning via Circular Convolution
methods.formula_latex: W = W_0 + \Delta W,\quad \Delta W = \big[\,\mathcal{C}(w_{ij})\,\big]_{i\le d_{out}/b,\ j\le d_{in}/b},\ \mathcal{C}(w)\in\mathbb{R}^{b\times b}\ \text{circulant with first row } w\in\mathbb{R}^{b}\ (\text{trained});\ \mathcal{C}(w) = F\,\mathrm{diag}\big(\tfrac{1}{b}Fw\big)F^{-1},\ \text{so } \Delta W x \text{ is computed blockwise with FFTs}
methods.trainable_params: \tfrac{d_{in}\,d_{out}}{b}
methods.locus: any linear layer whose dimensions are divisible by the block size b (paper: RoBERTa, LLaMA-3-8B, ViT)
methods.structure: block-circulant update: each b x b block is a circulant matrix (simultaneously diagonalised by the DFT), so rank can reach min(d_{in}, d_{out}) independently of the parameter count
methods.mergeable_reason: The block-circulant matrix can be materialised and added to W_0.
methods.identity_at_init: HF default initialises the kernels with xavier_uniform (non-zero, so not an exact identity); init_weights=True sets them to zero (no-op)
methods.key_idea: Use circular convolution (a circulant matrix) as the update: rank is decoupled from parameter count, and FFTs make forward and backward passes fast and memory-light; block-circulant structure handles non-square weights and tunes the budget.
methods.results_note: Consistently outperforms LoRA and its variants across fine-tuning tasks (e.g. on LLaMA-3-8B) while being efficient in compute and memory.

relations.note: both use the DFT; C3A makes Delta W DFT-diagonalisable rather than sparse in the 2-D spectrum
high-rank update with LoRA-like efficiency

papers.title: Measuring the Intrinsic Dimension of Objective Landscapes
papers.claim: Training in a random low-dimensional subspace theta = theta_0 + P theta_d reveals an intrinsic dimension at which solutions first appear; it is often far smaller than the parameter count and nearly constant across model sizes for a given task.
papers.relevance: Founding statement of the random-subspace view behind every member of this family: VeRA, NOLA, RandLoRA, Uni-LoRA and TinyLoRA are all choices of a (structured) random projection P into some parameter space.

papers.title: Asymmetry in Low-Rank Adapters of Foundation Models
papers.claim: In BA adapters, A extracts features and B maps them to outputs; tuning B is inherently more effective, a random untrained A performs nearly as well as a tuned one, and training only B tightens an information-theoretic generalisation bound.
papers.relevance: Theoretical justification for freezing, randomising or sharing one LoRA factor (VeRA, ShareLoRA, Lily, MiSS's fixed summing projection, LoRA-FA).

papers.title: PRANC: Pseudo RAndom Networks for Compacting deep models
papers.claim: A deep model can be reparameterised as a linear combination of several frozen, randomly initialised basis networks, so it can be stored as one seed plus mixture coefficients, compressing classifiers about 100x.
papers.relevance: Direct ancestor of NOLA (and of seed-regenerated bases in VeRA/RandLoRA): storage reduces to coefficients plus an RNG seed, a free-module view of the update space.

papers.title: Compressing Neural Networks with the Hashing Trick
papers.claim: Randomly grouping connection weights with a hash function so that each group shares one parameter (HashedNets) gives large compression with little accuracy loss.
papers.relevance: Random weight sharing is the mechanism behind Uni-LoRA's one-hot projection and MoSA's random tessellation; it frames sharing as a quotient of parameter space by a random partition.

notes: Scope: 28 methods in five sub-clusters. (1) Frozen random bases with learned coefficients or scalings: VeRA, PVeRA, NOLA, RandLoRA, Intrinsic SAID. (2) Cross-layer or intra-layer sharing and tying: Tied-LoRA, ShareLoRA, PRoLoRA, MoS, VB-LoRA, Uni-LoRA, Lily, RaSA, FacT, MoSA, MiSS. (3) Tiny trainable cores inside frozen weight-derived or random bases: LoRA-XS, LoRA-SB, TinyLoRA, LaMDA, LoRA-Mini, SVFT, FRoD. (4) Transform-domain sparse updates: FourierFT, WaveFT, SSH, LoCA, C3A. Unifying observation: almost every method here is Delta W = Phi(P theta) with frozen P (random, SVD-derived, DFT/DCT/DHT/DWT, index or tiling maps) and a small trainable theta; Uni-LoRA states this projection view explicitly for LoRA-space variants. Uncertainties: (a) Identity at init is not exact for VB-LoRA, Uni-LoRA, LoRA-XS (sigma=1e-5), SVFT (official code), FourierFT (paper default), SSH (Kaiming), C3A (HF default xavier), LoRA-Mini (Kaiming on all matrices) and LoRA-SB (starts at an approximate first full-FT step by design). (b) The NOLA paper does not specify coefficient initialisation; we report the README example. (c) MoSA (ICLR 2026): no arXiv id found; lambda initialisation not found in the text. (d) Lily trainable-parameter count is approximate (router placement varies). (e) FRoD: whether the diagonal Sigma_i is trained alongside the sparse S_i is inferred from the paper's Delta Sigma_i term and HF description (medium confidence). (f) Several statements marked 'our observation' are derived algebraically rather than claimed by the authors (MiSS = LoRA with frozen block-summing A; LoRA-XS as a special case of SVFT; NOLA in the Uni-LoRA template). (g) LaMDA and LoRA-XS formulas are converted from the papers' row-vector convention; the trainable core then sits next to Sigma_r, an equivalent reparameterisation. Venues checked: MiSS is ICLR 2026 (proceedings PDF checked); LoRA-XS is ECAI 2025; LaMDA is EMNLP 2024 Findings; C3A is ACL 2025 Findings; Lily is ACL 2025 Findings; SSH is NAACL 2025; PRoLoRA is ACL 2024; Tied-LoRA is NAACL 2024. A web-search summary claimed ShareLoRA and LoRA-SB were at ICLR 2026; the ICLR 2026 proceedings list (5,351 titles) contains neither, so both are recorded as arXiv (LoRA-SB also appeared at the ICLR 2025 SCOPE workshop). WaveFT, TinyLoRA, ShareLoRA and LoRA-Mini have no confirmed venue. HF PEFT (v0.21.1, 2026-09-29) implements VeRA, PVeRA, VB-LoRA, Uni-LoRA, RandLoRA, FourierFT, WaveFT, C3A, MiSS (Bone was removed in favour of MiSS), Lily, TinyLoRA and FRoD. Overlaps with other family files: svft (multiplicative), fact/c3a/miss (shape), lora-sb (init-rank), and the hf-peft list. Considered but excluded as low-uptake or better placed elsewhere: ASLoRA (arXiv 2412.10135), E2LoRA (ICLR 2026, entropy-guided adaptive cross-layer sharing), EigenLoRAx (CVPRW 2025, principal subspaces recycled from trained adapters), MASA (arXiv 2510.06005), LoTR/LoRETTA/Compacter/HyperFormer (tensor/adapter families), SHiRA (selective), ETHER/RoAd (multiplicative), HydraLoRA (composition).
